messages:
Ethan Wu: noticing two annoying behaviors in the python SDK error surface: 1) when the retry middleware wraps an HTTPError the original status_code and raw_body are lost (we only see RetryError), and 2) async stack traces drop the original request context so it's hard to map to customer code. both hit our sample-app onboarding tests.
Nora Gomez: hmm we intentionally wrap to simplify retry logic, but we should definitely preserve the original exception as `__cause__` and expose the `origin` attr on RetryError. do you have a tiny repro?
Ethan Wu: repro sketch:
```py
from redwood import Client, RetryError

async with Client(retries=2) as c:
    await c.post('/v1/generate', json={"prompt":"x"})
# currently raises RetryError('request failed') with no status_code or body
```
I tried catching `except RetryError as e: print(e.__cause__)` but it's None.
Jules Rivera: ack. parity note: sync transport preserves `e.__cause__` because exceptions are chained naturally in requests adapter; async path has an await boundary where we rewrap without chaining. that looks like a bug.
Nora Gomez: proposed changes: (a) make the retry wrapper re-raise using `raise RetryError(...) from original_exc`, (b) add `RetryError.original` (typing: Optional[APIError]) and `APIError` typed fields: `status_code: Optional[int]`, `raw_body: Optional[bytes]`, `text: Optional[str]`, `request_id: Optional[str]`, `method: Optional[str]`, `url: Optional[str]`, `raw_body_truncated: Optional[bool]`. docstring examples for mypy users.
Ethan Wu: +1. also, for async stack traces it'd help to include `client_request_trace` metadata in the exception (a tiny human readable snippet: METHOD URL <first-256-bytes-of-body>). this solves the onboarding scenario where folks paste a stack and we can't find the failing call.
Jules Rivera: small caveat: don't leak secrets; for bodies we should redact tokens and only include first 256 bytes. maybe a helper `redact_body_snippet(body_bytes)`.
Ethan Wu: agreed. I'd also like a helper `to_dict()` on APIError for quick telemetry upload in sample-apps so customers can copy-paste sanitized payloads into support tickets.
Nora Gomez: will implement: preserve raw_body up to 64KB, add `raw_body_truncated` flag, add `to_dict(redact=True)` which returns strings only. typing changes in `sdk/errors.py` and propagate to `__all__`.
ci-bot: Policy check: PR #5010 requires CLA signoff from @Nora Gomez :rotating_light:
Jules Rivera: I'll draft the PR and tests. tests: ensure RetryError.__cause__ is set, ensure APIError.raw_body kept for async `async with` context manager, non-utf8 decode returns `text` with replacement chars, redact helper strips Authorization/Bearer tokens.
Ethan Wu: can we also add a quickstart example showing recommended pattern? e.g.
```py
try:
    await client.create(...)
except APIError as e:
    print(e.status_code, e.text)
    j = e.json()  # helper
    if j and 'errors' in j:
        handle_validation(j['errors'])
    raise
```
that will reduce support churn.
Nora Gomez: good idea. I'll update docs/quickstart/error-handling.md and add a tiny sample-app change referencing it.
ci-bot: PR #5010 opened by Jules Rivera: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/5010 (checks: +5 -1).
Ethan Wu: ran the sample-app smoke locally with the branch, non-utf8 body test passes. thanks. :thumbsup:
Jules Rivera: one last note: we should semver-minor bump and call out exception typing and retry semantics in the changelog. also add migration blurb: users who `except RetryError` can inspect `e.original` or `e.__cause__` for status.
Nora Gomez: filed follow-up issue for telemetry-integrations to consume `APIError.to_dict()` in support tooling. https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-issues/1123
Ethan Wu: great. this should make onboarding less painful for customers seeing opaque retry errors.
ci-bot: CI for #5010 passed, merging... :white_check_mark:
